title: Exclusive | Gas Exporter Venture Global Wants to Get In on AI Power Boom
source_used: OilPrice.com article (author Charles Kennedy) read on Yahoo Finance
key_facts: Venture Global, a US exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG), signed agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes for up to 16 power generation units of 720 megawatts each.
The units could add about 11.5 gigawatts of capacity and support its aim of up to 10 GW of AI computing capacity by the end of 2034.
It already has about 4.5 GW of modular gas-fired power capacity, built, under construction or on order at its LNG sites.
The plants would run apart from the public grid and supply data centers on land the company owns or controls.
A regulatory filing puts the combined equipment deals at about $17.2 billion if all contemplated purchases go ahead; most purchases remain conditional.
The first power island purchase order is expected by the end of 2026.
quote_evidence: The agreements cover up to 16 power generation units, each with a capacity of 720 megawatts (MW), along with associated electrical infrastructure.

Venture Global expects to place its first power island purchase order by the end of 2026, with subsequent investments dependent on customer commitments, market demand, and other commercial considerations.
why_it_matters_hint: The company is trying to turn gas plants built for LNG into private power supplies for AI data centers, away from strained public grids.
notes: WSJ original (exclusive) was blocked (HTTP 401); Reuters also carried the equipment deals. Read the OilPrice text via Yahoo Finance. Most equipment purchases are conditional.
